title: Envelope
description: Every message that can cross the transport, tagged by `type`.

Batch.description: A bounded batch of envelopes, applied in order. Batches never nest.

BlobStart.description:
Announces a binary blob stream whose bytes follow as blob-chunk frames
(never base64 inside an envelope). Sent by whichever side streams the
blob; `request_id` ties the stream to its request.

sha256.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the full blob, when known, for end-to-end
integrity verification.

streamId.description: Stream id carried by each chunk frame; unique per session generation.

totalBytes.description: Total size when known up front, letting the receiver preflight bounds.

Cancel.description:
Cooperative cancellation of an in-flight request. The engine still sends
a terminal response for the id (`CANCELLED` if cancellation won).

ErrorCode.description:
Stable machine error codes. The wire form is the SCREAMING_SNAKE string;
codes are append-only once the protocol freezes.

oneOf.description: The `hello` auth token did not match the parent-issued token.
The peer speaks a protocol version outside our supported range.

A frame violated the framing layer (bad magic, unknown type, bad
flags, or a size bound).

A well-framed envelope violated a wire bound (string, collection,
batch, depth, or integer range).
A control frame did not decode into a known envelope.
The request method is not known to this engine build.
The request params failed method-level validation.
The request deadline elapsed before the engine finished.
The request was cancelled by the client or by session teardown.
Bounded queues are full; explicit backpressure.
The session generation is no longer valid (engine restarted).
The workspace handle does not refer to an open workspace.
Internal engine failure; details in redacted diagnostics only.

ErrorEnvelope.description: A failed response, or a connection-level error when `id` is absent.

Event.description:
An engine-initiated event. Events are totally ordered per session by
`seq`; a client that observes a gap must treat its state as stale and
resynchronize.

Hello.description:
First message on a connection, client → engine. Authenticates the
parent-child session: the desktop main process spawns the engine with a
random token in its environment and must echo it here. Anything before a
valid `hello` is answered with `AUTH_FAILED` and the connection closes.

lastSessionGeneration.description:
On reconnect after an engine restart: the generation the client last
saw, so the engine can tell resume-after-restart from first contact.
The engine always issues a fresh generation in `helloAck`.

capabilities.description: Intersection-negotiated capabilities in effect for this session.

limits.description: Bounds this engine enforces; the client must stay within them.

sessionGeneration.description:
Fresh per accepted connection. Old workspace handles, request ids and
event sequences are invalid under a new generation.

deadlineMs.description:
Relative deadline. The engine clamps it to its maximum and fails the
request with `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` when it elapses.

idempotencyKey.description:
Required on retryable mutations: the engine deduplicates replays of
the same key after timeouts/reconnects (exactly-once acknowledgement).

method.description:
Namespaced method name, e.g. `workspace.open`. Test-build fault
injection uses the reserved `testkit.` namespace.

params.description:
Method-specific parameters; validated per-method behind the envelope
layer, bounded here as a JSON tree.

workspace.description: Target workspace, when the method is workspace-scoped.

Response.description: A successful response to a request.

Retryability.description: How a generated client may retry a failed request.

oneOf.description: Retry with backoff (same session); pair with an idempotency key.
Re-handshake (new session generation, re-open handles), then retry.

WireError.description:
The wire error payload carried by an `error` envelope.

`message` must be redaction-safe: no paths, no document content, no
secrets, no tokens. Construct via [`WireError::new`] and keep messages to
static, code-like descriptions; anything dynamic belongs in structured
redacted diagnostics, not here.

WireLimits.description:
Bounds enforced by both encoder and decoder, and advertised to the client
in `helloAck` so both sides agree on what a well-formed peer may send.

maxBatchLen.description: Maximum number of envelopes in one `batch` envelope.

maxBlobChunkBytes.description:
Maximum blob-chunk payload size in bytes (raw bytes, excluding the
8-byte stream-id prefix).

maxCollectionLen.description: Maximum length of any array or object on the wire.

maxFrameBytes.description: Maximum control-frame payload size in bytes (the encoded envelope).

maxJsonDepth.description: Maximum nesting depth of any JSON value on the wire.

maxStringBytes.description: Maximum size of any single string on the wire, in UTF-8 bytes.

WorkspaceHandle.description:
Opaque, server-issued workspace handle. Clients never fabricate one and
never learn filesystem paths from it; handles die with their session
generation.
